subject.name: Chemistry
subject.description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry. Core students take Papers 1 and 3; Extended students take Papers 2 and 4. The practical papers (5 and 6) are not included. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: States of matter
topics.summary: Solids, liquids and gases, changes of state, diffusion.

topics.title: Atoms, elements and compounds
topics.summary: Atomic structure, isotopes, ions and ionic bonds, covalent bonds, giant structures, metallic bonding.

topics.title: Stoichiometry
topics.summary: Formulae, equations, relative masses and the mole.

topics.title: Chemical energetics
topics.summary: Exothermic and endothermic reactions, bond energies.

topics.title: Chemical reactions
topics.summary: Physical and chemical changes, rate of reaction, reversible reactions and equilibrium, redox.

topics.title: Acids, bases and salts
topics.summary: Properties of acids and bases, oxides, preparation of salts.

topics.title: The Periodic Table
topics.summary: Arrangement of elements, Group I, Group VII, transition elements, noble gases.

topics.title: Metals
topics.summary: Properties and uses, alloys, reactivity series, corrosion, extraction.

topics.title: Chemistry of the environment
topics.summary: Water, fertilisers, air quality and climate.

topics.title: Organic chemistry
topics.summary: Formulae and homologous series, alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, polymers.

topics.title: Experimental techniques and chemical analysis
topics.summary: Experimental design, titrations, chromatography, separation and purification, identification of ions and gases.

parts.prompt: Which change of state is a solid turning directly into a gas?
parts.examinerComment: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas, as with solid carbon dioxide.

parts.prompt: Which gas diffuses fastest at the same temperature?
parts.examinerComment: Gases with a lower relative molecular mass diffuse faster. Hydrogen has Mᵣ = 2.

parts.prompt: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its nucleon number?
parts.examinerComment: Nucleon number = protons + neutrons.

parts.prompt: Which substance has a giant covalent structure?
parts.examinerComment: Sodium chloride is giant ionic; methane is simple molecular; copper is metallic.

parts.prompt: What is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃?
What volume does {n} mol of a gas occupy at room temperature and pressure?
parts.examinerComment: One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ at r.t.p., so volume = {n} × 24 = {=n*24} dm³.

parts.prompt: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed. What forms at the cathode?
parts.examinerComment: Positive lead ions are attracted to the negative cathode and gain electrons.

parts.prompt: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed. What forms at the anode?
parts.examinerComment: Hydrogen forms at the cathode. Sodium is never produced from aqueous solutions.

parts.prompt: What happens to the temperature of the surroundings during an exothermic reaction?
parts.examinerComment: Exothermic reactions transfer thermal energy to the surroundings.

parts.prompt: Which statement about bonds is correct?
parts.examinerComment: Energy is needed to break bonds; energy is released when bonds form.

parts.prompt: Why does increasing the temperature increase the rate of a reaction?

options.text: Particles have more kinetic energy, so there are more frequent successful collisions.
The concentration of the reactants increases.

markingPoints.text: C – Particles have more kinetic energy, so there are more frequent successful collisions.

parts.examinerComment: Answers should refer to more collisions per second with energy greater than the activation energy.

parts.prompt: What is oxidation in terms of electrons?
parts.examinerComment: Remember OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain.

parts.prompt: What is the pH of a neutral solution?
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Which salt is made when dilute sulfuric acid reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
parts.examinerComment: Sulfuric acid forms sulfates; sulfides contain no oxygen.

parts.prompt: How does the reactivity of Group I metals change down the group?
parts.examinerComment: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and is lost more easily.

parts.prompt: Why are the noble gases unreactive?

options.text: They have a full outer shell of electrons.

markingPoints.text: B – They have a full outer shell of electrons.

parts.examinerComment: Noble gases are monatomic, so option D is wrong.

parts.prompt: Which metal is extracted from bauxite by electrolysis?
parts.examinerComment: Iron and zinc are extracted by reduction with carbon.

parts.prompt: What is needed for iron to rust?
parts.examinerComment: Experiments with drying agents and boiled water show both are needed.

parts.prompt: Which gas is the main cause of acid rain?
parts.examinerComment: Carbon dioxide contributes to climate change, not significantly to acid rain.

parts.prompt: Approximately what percentage of clean, dry air is nitrogen?
parts.examinerComment: Oxygen is about 21%.

parts.prompt: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
parts.examinerComment: CₙH₂ₙ is the general formula of the alkenes.

parts.prompt: Which observation shows that a hydrocarbon is an alkene?

options.text: It burns with a blue flame.

parts.examinerComment: Aqueous bromine changes from orange to colourless.

parts.prompt: Which method separates sand from water?
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: How is the Rf value in chromatography calculated?

options.text: distance moved by solvent ÷ distance moved by substance
distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by solvent
distance moved by substance − distance moved by solvent
distance moved by substance × distance moved by solvent

markingPoints.text: B – distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by solvent

parts.examinerComment: Rf values are always less than 1.

parts.prompt: Describe the arrangement and motion of the particles in a liquid.

markingPoints.text: close together, in an irregular (random) arrangement
particles move / slide past each other

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates described a gas. Liquid particles are still touching.

parts.prompt: An atom of chlorine is represented by ³⁷₁₇Cl. State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in this atom.
parts.examinerComment: The neutron number is 37 − 17.

parts.prompt: Calculate the relative formula mass of ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄.
parts.examinerComment: Multiplying the whole NH₄ group by 2 was essential.

parts.prompt: State what is meant by electrolysis.

markingPoints.text: when molten or in aqueous solution, by the passage of an electric current

parts.examinerComment: Answers must state that the compound is broken down.

parts.prompt: The temperature of a reaction mixture rises from 21 °C to 34 °C. State the temperature change and whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Marble chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid. State two ways to increase the rate of this reaction.

markingPoints.text: increase the concentration of the acid

parts.examinerComment: 'Add more acid' is not the same as increasing its concentration.

parts.prompt: Name the gas produced when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, and give a test for it.

markingPoints.text: a lighted splint gives a squeaky pop

parts.examinerComment: A glowing splint is the test for oxygen.

parts.prompt: Name the two products formed when potassium reacts with water.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Explain why alloys are often used instead of pure metals.

markingPoints.text: different-sized atoms disrupt the layers so they cannot slide easily

parts.examinerComment: The best answers explained the structure as well as stating the property.

parts.prompt: Describe a chemical test for water.

markingPoints.text: turns from white to blue (or cobalt(II) chloride from blue to pink)

parts.examinerComment: Both the reagent and the colour change are needed.

parts.prompt: Name the functional group present in ethanol.
parts.examinerComment: 'Hydroxide' is incorrect: that is an ion.

parts.prompt: In a chromatography experiment, a spot moves {s} cm and the solvent front moves {f} cm. Calculate the Rf value.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates divided correctly. Rf values have no units and are always less than 1.

questions.stem: A solid is heated steadily. Fig. 1 shows how its temperature changes.

figures.alt: Heating curve: temperature rises from 20 °C to 80 °C in 4 minutes, stays at 80 °C until 9 minutes, then rises to 130 °C at 14 minutes.
figures.caption: Fig. 1

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use Fig. 1 to find the melting point of the substance, in °C.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the temperature stays constant between 4 and 9 minutes.

markingPoints.text: energy is used to overcome the forces between particles instead of raising the temperature

parts.examinerComment: Many said 'no energy is being supplied', but heating continues throughout.

questions.stem: Marble chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid. Fig. 2 shows the volume of carbon dioxide collected.

figures.alt: Graph of volume of gas against time: the volume rises steeply at first, then levels off at 60 cm³ after about 60 s.
figures.caption: Fig. 2

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use Fig. 2 to find the total volume of gas produced, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use Fig. 2 to find the volume of gas collected after 20 s, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Read carefully from the curve.

questions.stem: Fig. 3 shows the chromatogram of two dyes, A and B, and a mixture, X.

figures.alt: Chromatogram: the solvent front is 8.0 cm above the baseline. Dye A gives one spot at 2.0 cm, dye B one spot at 6.0 cm, and mixture X two spots at 2.0 cm and 6.0 cm.
figures.caption: Fig. 3

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Which dyes does mixture X contain? Explain your answer.

markingPoints.text: its spots are at the same heights as the spots of A and B

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the Rf value of dye A.
parts.examinerComment: Measure from the baseline, not the bottom of the paper.

parts.prompt: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases are released at opposite ends of a long tube. A white ring of ammonium chloride forms nearer the hydrogen chloride end. Explain why.

markingPoints.text: ammonia has a lower Mᵣ (17) than hydrogen chloride (36.5)
so ammonia travels further before the gases meet

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should compare relative molecular masses using numbers.

parts.prompt: Explain why sodium chloride has a high melting point.

markingPoints.text: strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
a lot of energy is needed to overcome these forces

parts.examinerComment: References to 'strong bonds' without saying what type did not earn full credit.

parts.prompt: Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of calcium oxide formed from {m} g of calcium carbonate, in g.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. Candidates who used Mr(CaO) = 56 and the 1 : 1 ratio scored full marks.

parts.prompt: Write the ionic half-equation for the reaction at the cathode when copper is deposited from aqueous copper(II) sulfate.

markingPoints.text: Cu²⁺ and e⁻ on the left, Cu on the right

parts.examinerComment: Electrons must be gained at the cathode.

parts.prompt: Use the bond energies to calculate the energy change for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl, in kJ/mol. Bond energies: H–H 436, Cl–Cl 242, H–Cl 431 kJ/mol.
parts.examinerComment: The negative sign shows the reaction is exothermic and is required.

parts.prompt: In the Haber process, N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ and the forward reaction is exothermic. State and explain the effect on the yield of ammonia of increasing the pressure.

markingPoints.text: the position of equilibrium shifts to the right
because there are fewer moles of gas on the right (2 compared with 4)

parts.examinerComment: Answers should refer to the number of moles of gas on each side.

parts.prompt: 25.0 cm³ of aqueous sodium hydroxide is neutralised by {v} cm³ of {c} mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. Calculate the concentration of the sodium hydroxide, in mol/dm³.
parts.examinerComment: Converting cm³ to dm³ was the most common source of error.

parts.prompt: Chlorine is bubbled into aqueous potassium bromide. Explain what happens and write the ionic equation.

markingPoints.text: chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces it

parts.examinerComment: Potassium ions are spectator ions and are left out of the ionic equation.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced equation for the reduction of iron(III) oxide by carbon monoxide in the blast furnace.

markingPoints.text: correct formulae: Fe₂O₃, CO, Fe, CO₂

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Explain how a catalytic converter reduces air pollution from car engines.

markingPoints.text: carbon monoxide is converted to carbon dioxide
oxides of nitrogen are converted to nitrogen

parts.examinerComment: Both pollutants and their products were needed for full marks.

parts.prompt: Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol to form an ester. Name the ester and state the conditions needed.

markingPoints.text: concentrated sulfuric acid as a catalyst, with heating

parts.examinerComment: 'Ethanoyl ethanol' and 'ethyl ethanol' were common incorrect names.

parts.prompt: Describe a test for ammonium ions in a solution.

markingPoints.text: add aqueous sodium hydroxide and warm
which turns damp red litmus paper blue

parts.examinerComment: The litmus paper must be damp.

questions.stem: Marble chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid. Fig. 2 shows the volume of carbon dioxide collected.

figures.alt: Graph of volume of gas against time: the volume rises steeply at first, then levels off at 60 cm³ after about 60 s.
figures.caption: Fig. 2

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain, in terms of particles, why the rate of reaction decreases as the reaction proceeds.

markingPoints.text: the concentration of acid decreases / fewer acid particles
so there are fewer collisions per second

parts.examinerComment: Answers should refer to the frequency of collisions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On the same axes, a student repeats the experiment with powdered marble of the same mass. Describe how the new curve would differ.

markingPoints.text: levels off at the same final volume, 60 cm³

parts.examinerComment: The final volume depends on the amount of reactants, not the rate.

questions.stem: Fig. 3 shows the chromatogram of two dyes, A and B, and a mixture, X.

figures.alt: Chromatogram: the solvent front is 8.0 cm above the baseline. Dye A gives one spot at 2.0 cm, dye B one spot at 6.0 cm, and mixture X two spots at 2.0 cm and 6.0 cm.
figures.caption: Fig. 3

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the Rf value of dye B.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the baseline must be drawn in pencil, not ink.

markingPoints.text: ink would dissolve in the solvent and separate, giving extra spots

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Which statement describes the particles in a gas?

options.text: close together and vibrating about fixed positions
far apart and moving randomly at high speed
far apart and held in fixed positions

markingPoints.text: C – far apart and moving randomly at high speed

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates confused the description of a liquid (close together, moving randomly) with that of a gas.

parts.prompt: A balloon filled with air is warmed. The pressure stays the same. What happens to the volume of the air?

options.text: It decreases because the particles get smaller.
It increases because the particles move faster and further apart.
It stays the same because the number of particles is unchanged.
It increases because the particles get bigger.

markingPoints.text: B – It increases because the particles move faster and further apart.

parts.examinerComment: The particles themselves do not change size; they gain kinetic energy and the gas expands.

parts.prompt: Which statement about the atoms ¹²₆C and ¹⁴₆C is correct?

options.text: They have the same number of neutrons.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
They have different numbers of electrons.

markingPoints.text: B – They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

parts.examinerComment: Isotopes have the same number of protons and electrons, so they have the same chemical properties.

parts.prompt: What is the electronic configuration of a magnesium atom?
parts.examinerComment: Magnesium has 12 electrons. The first shell holds 2 and the second shell holds 8.

parts.prompt: Which pair of elements forms a covalent compound?
parts.examinerComment: Covalent bonds form between non-metal atoms. The other pairs are a metal and a non-metal, which form ionic compounds.

parts.prompt: What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
parts.examinerComment: Al³⁺ and O²⁻ ions combine in the ratio 2 : 3 so that the charges balance.

parts.prompt: Which equation is correctly balanced?
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should check that there are the same number of atoms of each element on both sides, without changing formulae.

parts.prompt: 24 g of magnesium burns to form 40 g of magnesium oxide. What mass of magnesium oxide forms when {m} g of magnesium burns?
parts.examinerComment: The mass of magnesium oxide is 40/24 times the mass of magnesium: {m} × 40 ÷ 24 = {=m*5/3} g.

parts.prompt: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity?

options.text: Its ions are not free to move.

markingPoints.text: B – Its ions are not free to move.

parts.examinerComment: Sodium chloride is made of ions held in a lattice. The ions can only move when it is molten or dissolved.

parts.prompt: Dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed using inert electrodes. Which products form at the cathode and at the anode?
parts.examinerComment: Positive hydrogen ions are attracted to the negative cathode. Oxygen is formed at the anode.

parts.prompt: A metal spoon is electroplated with silver. Which arrangement is used?

options.text: spoon as the anode; aqueous silver nitrate as the electrolyte
spoon as the cathode; aqueous silver nitrate as the electrolyte
spoon as the cathode; aqueous sodium chloride as the electrolyte
spoon as the anode; aqueous copper(II) sulfate as the electrolyte

markingPoints.text: B – spoon as the cathode; aqueous silver nitrate as the electrolyte

parts.examinerComment: The object to be plated is the cathode, and the electrolyte must contain ions of the plating metal.

parts.prompt: Which process is endothermic?

options.text: neutralising an acid with an alkali
the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate

markingPoints.text: C – the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate

parts.examinerComment: Thermal decomposition needs a continuous supply of heat. The other reactions release energy.

parts.prompt: In the reaction pathway diagram for an exothermic reaction, how does the energy of the products compare with that of the reactants?

options.text: The products have less energy than the reactants.
The products have more energy than the reactants.
The products and reactants have the same energy.

markingPoints.text: A – The products have less energy than the reactants.

parts.examinerComment: Energy is released to the surroundings, so the products are lower on the diagram.

parts.prompt: When ammonium nitrate dissolves in water, the temperature changes from {t} °C to {=t-d} °C. Which row is correct?
parts.examinerComment: The temperature falls by {t} − {=t-d} = {d} °C, so energy is taken in from the surroundings: the process is endothermic.

parts.prompt: Which change is a chemical change?
parts.examinerComment: Burning magnesium forms a new substance, magnesium oxide. The other changes are physical and can easily be reversed.

parts.prompt: Which statement about a catalyst is correct?

options.text: It increases the rate of reaction and is used up.
It increases the rate of reaction and is unchanged at the end.
It increases the yield of product.
It slows down the reverse reaction only.

markingPoints.text: B – It increases the rate of reaction and is unchanged at the end.

parts.examinerComment: A catalyst is chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction.

parts.prompt: Which oxide is acidic?
parts.examinerComment: Oxides of non-metals are usually acidic; metal oxides are basic.

parts.prompt: What colour is universal indicator in a solution with a pH of 13?
parts.examinerComment: Strongly alkaline solutions turn universal indicator purple (violet).

parts.prompt: Which pair of substances can be used to make copper(II) sulfate crystals?

options.text: copper(II) oxide and dilute sulfuric acid
copper(II) oxide and dilute hydrochloric acid

markingPoints.text: B – copper(II) oxide and dilute sulfuric acid

parts.examinerComment: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series and does not react with dilute acids, so a base such as copper(II) oxide is used.

parts.prompt: Element X is in Group II and Period 3 of the Periodic Table. What is X?
parts.examinerComment: Period 3 elements have three occupied electron shells; Group II elements have two outer-shell electrons.

parts.prompt: Which statement about the Group VII elements is correct?

options.text: They become lighter in colour down the group.
Chlorine is a pale yellow-green gas at room temperature.
Iodine is a liquid at room temperature.
Their reactivity increases down the group.

markingPoints.text: B – Chlorine is a pale yellow-green gas at room temperature.

parts.examinerComment: Bromine is a red-brown liquid and iodine is a grey-black solid. Reactivity decreases down the group.

parts.prompt: Which property is typical of a transition element?
parts.examinerComment: Transition elements have high densities and high melting points, and they and their compounds often act as catalysts.

parts.prompt: Which metal is the most reactive?
parts.examinerComment: Calcium is near the top of the reactivity series, above zinc, iron and copper.

parts.prompt: Why is aluminium used to make aircraft bodies?

options.text: It has a low density and resists corrosion.
It is a good conductor of heat.

markingPoints.text: B – It has a low density and resists corrosion.

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should link the property to the use: a light, strong, corrosion-resistant metal is needed.

parts.prompt: Which treatment does NOT help to stop an iron gate from rusting?

options.text: washing it regularly with salt water

markingPoints.text: C – washing it regularly with salt water

parts.examinerComment: Salt water speeds up rusting. The other methods stop water and oxygen reaching the iron.

parts.prompt: Which substance is added to drinking water to kill microbes?
parts.examinerComment: Carbon removes tastes and odours, and sand filters out solids; chlorination kills microbes.

parts.prompt: Which compound in a fertiliser supplies nitrogen to plants?
parts.examinerComment: Ammonium salts and nitrates supply nitrogen; potassium and phosphorus are supplied by other compounds.

parts.prompt: Which pair are both greenhouse gases?
parts.examinerComment: Carbon dioxide and methane absorb thermal energy radiated from the Earth's surface.

parts.prompt: What is formed when ethene reacts with steam in the presence of a catalyst?
parts.examinerComment: Steam adds across the C=C double bond to form ethanol.

parts.prompt: Which statement about the members of a homologous series is correct?

options.text: They have the same molecular formula.
They have the same functional group and similar chemical properties.
They have the same boiling point.
They have the same number of carbon atoms.

markingPoints.text: B – They have the same functional group and similar chemical properties.

parts.examinerComment: Members of a homologous series have the same general formula and show a trend in physical properties such as boiling point.

parts.prompt: Which fraction from petroleum is used as fuel for jet aircraft?
parts.examinerComment: Kerosene (paraffin) is jet fuel; gasoline is petrol for cars and bitumen is used to surface roads.

parts.prompt: Which test shows that a solution contains chloride ions?

options.text: Acidify with dilute nitric acid and add aqueous silver nitrate: a white precipitate forms.
Acidify with dilute nitric acid and add aqueous barium nitrate: a white precipitate forms.
Add aqueous sodium hydroxide and warm: a gas turns damp red litmus blue.
Add dilute hydrochloric acid: bubbles of gas turn limewater milky.

markingPoints.text: A – Acidify with dilute nitric acid and add aqueous silver nitrate: a white precipitate forms.

parts.examinerComment: Option B is the test for sulfate ions, C for ammonium ions and D for carbonate ions.

parts.prompt: Which piece of apparatus measures exactly 25.0 cm³ of a solution most accurately?
parts.examinerComment: A volumetric pipette delivers one fixed volume accurately. Burettes are used for variable volumes.

parts.prompt: Which change makes a gas diffuse more slowly?

options.text: using a gas with a lower relative molecular mass
using a gas with a higher relative molecular mass

markingPoints.text: C – using a gas with a higher relative molecular mass

parts.examinerComment: At the same temperature, particles with a higher relative molecular mass move more slowly.

parts.prompt: A fixed mass of gas is heated in a sealed container of fixed volume. Why does the pressure increase?

options.text: The particles move faster and hit the walls more often and with more force.
The particles attract each other less strongly.

markingPoints.text: B – The particles move faster and hit the walls more often and with more force.

parts.examinerComment: The number and size of the particles do not change.

parts.prompt: Why does the temperature of a pure solid stay constant while it melts?

options.text: The energy supplied is used to overcome the forces of attraction between the particles.
Energy is lost to the surroundings as fast as it is supplied.
The particles stop moving while they change state.
The kinetic energy of the particles increases.

markingPoints.text: A – The energy supplied is used to overcome the forces of attraction between the particles.

parts.examinerComment: Stronger candidates linked the energy supplied to overcoming attractive forces rather than to increasing particle speed.

parts.prompt: A sample of copper contains 69% ⁶³Cu and 31% ⁶⁵Cu. What is the relative atomic mass of copper in this sample?
parts.examinerComment: (63 × 69 + 65 × 31) ÷ 100 = 63.62. The answer must be closer to 63 because that isotope is more abundant.

parts.prompt: Which statement explains why metals conduct electricity?

options.text: Positive ions move through the metal.
They contain delocalised electrons that are free to move.
Their ions are free to move only when molten.

markingPoints.text: B – They contain delocalised electrons that are free to move.

parts.examinerComment: Metallic bonding is the attraction between a lattice of positive ions and a 'sea' of delocalised electrons.

parts.prompt: Why does silicon(IV) oxide have a very high melting point?

options.text: Many strong covalent bonds must be broken throughout its giant structure.

markingPoints.text: C – Many strong covalent bonds must be broken throughout its giant structure.

parts.examinerComment: Silicon(IV) oxide has a giant covalent structure similar to diamond.

parts.prompt: Calcium carbonate reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. What volume of carbon dioxide, measured at r.t.p., is produced from {m} g of calcium carbonate?
parts.examinerComment: Moles CaCO₃ = {m} ÷ 100 = {=m/100}; moles CO₂ = {=m/100}; volume = {=m/100} × 24 = {=0.24*m} dm³.

parts.prompt: A hydrocarbon contains 75% carbon and 25% hydrogen by mass. What is its empirical formula?
parts.examinerComment: 75 ÷ 12 = 6.25 and 25 ÷ 1 = 25, a ratio of 1 : 4. C₃H comes from forgetting to divide by the relative atomic masses.

parts.prompt: Which sample contains the greatest number of molecules?

markingPoints.text: C – 88 g of carbon dioxide, CO₂

parts.examinerComment: 88 ÷ 44 = 2 mol; the others are 1 mol, 1 mol and 0.5 mol.

parts.prompt: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃?
parts.examinerComment: Mr = 80 and there are two nitrogen atoms: 28 ÷ 80 × 100 = 35.0%. Answer A counts only one nitrogen atom.

parts.prompt: Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is electrolysed using copper electrodes. Which half-equation shows the reaction at the anode?
parts.examinerComment: With copper electrodes, the copper anode dissolves, losing electrons to form copper(II) ions.

parts.prompt: Dilute aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed using inert electrodes. What is the main product at the anode?
parts.examinerComment: In dilute solution, hydroxide ions are discharged at the anode to form oxygen. Concentrated solutions give chlorine.

parts.prompt: What is an advantage of hydrogen–oxygen fuel cells compared with petrol engines in cars?

options.text: The only chemical product is water.
Hydrogen can be produced without using any energy.

markingPoints.text: B – The only chemical product is water.

parts.examinerComment: Hydrogen is difficult to store and its production usually uses energy from fossil fuels.

parts.prompt: The energy change for a reaction is −92 kJ/mol. Which statement is correct?

options.text: More energy is released making bonds than is taken in breaking bonds.
More energy is taken in breaking bonds than is released making bonds.
The products have more energy than the reactants.

markingPoints.text: A – More energy is released making bonds than is taken in breaking bonds.

parts.examinerComment: A negative ΔH means the reaction is exothermic: bond making releases more energy than bond breaking absorbs.

parts.prompt: Methane burns: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O; ΔH = −890 kJ/mol. How much energy is released when {m} g of methane burns completely?
parts.examinerComment: Moles CH₄ = {m} ÷ 16 = {=m/16}; energy released = {=m/16} × 890 = {=890*m/16} kJ.

parts.prompt: Which process has a positive value of ΔH?
parts.examinerComment: Photosynthesis is endothermic: it takes in energy from light.

parts.prompt: In the Contact process, 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ and the forward reaction is exothermic. What happens to the equilibrium yield of SO₃ if the temperature is increased?
parts.examinerComment: Increasing the temperature favours the endothermic (backward) reaction, so the position of equilibrium moves to the left.

parts.prompt: Why does increasing the concentration of an acid increase the rate of its reaction with magnesium?

options.text: There are more collisions per second between reacting particles.

markingPoints.text: B – There are more collisions per second between reacting particles.

parts.examinerComment: More particles per unit volume gives a higher collision frequency; the energy of the particles does not change.

parts.prompt: In the reaction 2Fe²⁺ + Cl₂ → 2Fe³⁺ + 2Cl⁻, which substance is the oxidising agent?
parts.examinerComment: Chlorine gains electrons (it is reduced) and so oxidises the iron(II) ions.

parts.prompt: Which statement describes a weak acid?

options.text: an acid that has a low concentration
an acid that only partially dissociates in water
an acid with a pH of 7
an acid that fully dissociates in water

markingPoints.text: B – an acid that only partially dissociates in water

parts.examinerComment: Strength refers to the degree of dissociation, not to concentration.

parts.prompt: What is a base, in terms of protons?

options.text: a substance that produces H⁺ ions

parts.examinerComment: Acids are proton donors and bases are proton acceptors.

parts.prompt: Which oxide is amphoteric?
parts.examinerComment: Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis. Carbon monoxide is a neutral oxide.

parts.prompt: Astatine is below iodine in Group VII. Which prediction about astatine is correct?

options.text: It is a black solid that is less reactive than iodine.
It displaces iodine from aqueous potassium iodide.
It is more reactive than chlorine.

markingPoints.text: B – It is a black solid that is less reactive than iodine.

parts.examinerComment: Down Group VII, the elements become darker and less reactive.

parts.prompt: Iron forms two chlorides, FeCl₂ and FeCl₃. Which property of transition elements does this show?
parts.examinerComment: Iron has oxidation number +2 in FeCl₂ and +3 in FeCl₃.

parts.prompt: What do elements in the same period of the Periodic Table have in common?

options.text: the same number of outer-shell electrons
the same number of occupied electron shells

markingPoints.text: B – the same number of occupied electron shells

parts.examinerComment: Elements in the same group have the same number of outer-shell electrons and similar properties.

parts.prompt: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than by heating its oxide with carbon?

options.text: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon.
Aluminium is less reactive than carbon.
Aluminium oxide has a low melting point.

markingPoints.text: A – Aluminium is more reactive than carbon.

parts.examinerComment: Carbon can only reduce oxides of metals below it in the reactivity series.

parts.prompt: Blocks of zinc are attached to the steel hulls of ships. Why does this prevent rusting?

options.text: Zinc is less reactive than iron.
Zinc loses electrons more readily than iron, so it corrodes instead.
Zinc forms an alloy with the steel.
Zinc conducts heat away from the hull.

markingPoints.text: B – Zinc loses electrons more readily than iron, so it corrodes instead.

parts.examinerComment: This is sacrificial protection: the more reactive zinc is oxidised in preference to iron.

parts.prompt: What is the purpose of the limestone added to a blast furnace?

options.text: to form calcium oxide, which removes silicon(IV) oxide as slag
to reduce iron(III) oxide to iron

markingPoints.text: B – to form calcium oxide, which removes silicon(IV) oxide as slag

parts.examinerComment: Limestone decomposes to calcium oxide, a base, which reacts with acidic silicon(IV) oxide impurities.

parts.prompt: How are oxides of nitrogen formed in car engines?

options.text: Nitrogen and oxygen from the air react at the high temperature in the engine.

markingPoints.text: A – Nitrogen and oxygen from the air react at the high temperature in the engine.

parts.examinerComment: Petrol contains very little nitrogen; the nitrogen comes from the air drawn into the engine.

parts.prompt: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
parts.examinerComment: Plants take in carbon dioxide during photosynthesis. The other processes release it.

parts.prompt: Which method reduces the emission of sulfur dioxide from power stations?

options.text: flue gas desulfurisation using calcium oxide

markingPoints.text: B – flue gas desulfurisation using calcium oxide

parts.examinerComment: Calcium oxide is a base that reacts with acidic sulfur dioxide in the waste gases.

parts.prompt: Which is the structural formula of propanoic acid?
parts.examinerComment: Propanoic acid has three carbon atoms including the carbon in the COOH group.

parts.prompt: What type of reaction takes place when methane reacts with chlorine in ultraviolet light?
parts.examinerComment: A hydrogen atom is replaced by a chlorine atom. Alkanes cannot undergo addition reactions.

parts.prompt: Which pair of monomers can react together to form a polyester?

options.text: a diol and a dicarboxylic acid
a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid

markingPoints.text: A – a diol and a dicarboxylic acid

parts.examinerComment: A diamine and a dicarboxylic acid form a polyamide; amino acids form proteins.

parts.prompt: Aqueous sodium hydroxide is added to a solution. A green precipitate forms that does not dissolve in excess. Which ion is present?
parts.examinerComment: Cu²⁺ gives a light blue precipitate, Fe³⁺ red-brown and Zn²⁺ white, soluble in excess.

parts.prompt: A compound gives a lilac colour in a flame test. Which metal ion is present?
parts.examinerComment: Lithium gives red, sodium yellow and copper(II) blue-green.

parts.prompt: State the name of the process in which particles spread out from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates wrote 'evaporation' or 'dissolving', which are not correct.

parts.prompt: Describe and explain, using the kinetic particle theory, what happens to the volume of a gas when it is heated at constant pressure.

markingPoints.text: particles move further apart / take up more space
particles hit the walls harder or more often, pushing them out

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers referred to the movement of particles. Weaker answers stated wrongly that the particles themselves expand.

questions.stem: Magnesium reacts with chlorine to form magnesium chloride, MgCl₂.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe, in terms of electrons, how magnesium atoms and chlorine atoms form ions when they react.

markingPoints.text: each magnesium atom loses two electrons
each chlorine atom gains one electron
ions have full outer shells / noble gas configuration

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates stated that electrons are shared, which describes covalent bonding.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State the type of bonding in magnesium chloride.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Graphite is used to make electrodes. Explain, in terms of its structure, why graphite conducts electricity.

markingPoints.text: each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms
one electron per atom is free / delocalised and can move

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who wrote about 'free ions' did not score; graphite contains no ions.

questions.stem: Copper(II) carbonate decomposes when heated: CuCO₃ → CuO + CO₂.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A student heats {=1.24*k} g of copper(II) carbonate in an open crucible until the mass stops changing. {=1.6*k/2} g of copper(II) oxide remains. Calculate the mass of carbon dioxide given off, in g.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. A few candidates added the masses instead of subtracting.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suggest why the mass of the crucible and its contents decreases, even though mass is conserved in a chemical reaction.

markingPoints.text: carbon dioxide is a gas that escapes into the air

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should recognise that a product is lost from an open container.

parts.prompt: Calculate the relative formula mass of magnesium nitrate, Mg(NO₃)₂.
parts.examinerComment: The most common error was multiplying only the oxygen atoms by 2.

parts.prompt: In a blast furnace, 160 tonnes of iron(III) oxide produces 112 tonnes of iron. Calculate the mass of iron that can be produced from {m} tonnes of iron(III) oxide, in tonnes.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who set out the proportion clearly usually scored both marks.

parts.prompt: Write the formula of the compound formed between calcium ions, Ca²⁺, and chloride ions, Cl⁻.
parts.examinerComment: CaCl was a common error; the charges must balance.

questions.stem: Molten zinc chloride is electrolysed using graphite electrodes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Name the product formed at the cathode.
parts.examinerComment: Metals are formed at the cathode.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Describe what is seen at the anode.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates were asked for observations; naming chlorine alone did not score both marks.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why the zinc chloride must be molten for electrolysis to take place.

markingPoints.text: ions must be free to move
in the solid the ions are held in fixed positions / in a lattice

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers referred to ions, not electrons.

parts.prompt: State the two reactants used in a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell and the only chemical product.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered by most candidates.

questions.stem: Dilute hydrochloric acid is added to aqueous sodium hydroxide in a polystyrene cup.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: The temperature rises from {t} °C to {=t+d} °C. Calculate the temperature change, in °C.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State whether this reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
parts.examinerComment: A rise in temperature shows that energy is released to the surroundings.

parts.prompt: Describe how a reaction pathway diagram shows that a reaction is endothermic. Refer to the reactants, the products and the activation energy.

markingPoints.text: products are at a higher energy than the reactants
energy change arrow points upwards / ΔH is positive
activation energy shown as the rise from the reactants to the top of the curve

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates labelled the activation energy from the products, which is incorrect.

questions.stem: When blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate is heated, it forms anhydrous copper(II) sulfate and water. The reaction is reversible.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the colour of anhydrous copper(II) sulfate.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates gave 'colourless', which was not accepted for a solid.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Describe what is seen when water is added to anhydrous copper(II) sulfate, and state what this shows about the reaction.

markingPoints.text: the reaction can go in both directions / is reversible

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Magnesium ribbon reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. {v} cm³ of hydrogen is collected in the first {t} s. Calculate the average rate of reaction over this time, in cm³/s.
parts.examinerComment: A few candidates divided the time by the volume.

parts.prompt: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, identify the substance that is oxidised and the substance that is reduced. Give a reason for each.

markingPoints.text: hydrogen is oxidised because it gains oxygen
copper(II) oxide is reduced because it loses oxygen

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers gave a reason for each identification.

parts.prompt: Describe how to prepare a pure, dry sample of zinc sulfate crystals from zinc oxide and dilute sulfuric acid.

markingPoints.text: add excess zinc oxide to (warm) dilute sulfuric acid
filter to remove the excess zinc oxide
heat the filtrate to evaporate some water / to the crystallisation point
filter off the crystals and dry between filter papers

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates heated the solution to dryness, which does not give crystals of the hydrated salt.

parts.prompt: Name the salt formed when dilute nitric acid reacts with aqueous potassium hydroxide.
parts.examinerComment: Nitric acid forms nitrates; candidates who wrote 'potassium nitrite' did not score.

parts.prompt: Dilute hydrochloric acid is added to calcium carbonate. Describe what is seen and name the gas produced.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates named hydrogen, which is produced when acids react with metals.

questions.stem: Lithium, sodium and potassium are in Group I of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe what is seen when a small piece of sodium is added to cold water.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates were asked what is seen; 'hydrogen is produced' is not an observation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Rubidium is below potassium in Group I. Predict how the reaction of rubidium with water compares with that of potassium, and name the two products.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Argon is used to fill some light bulbs. Explain why.

markingPoints.text: the hot filament does not react / burn

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers related the unreactivity to the full outer shell of electrons.

parts.prompt: Astatine is below iodine in Group VII. Predict the physical state of astatine at room temperature.
parts.examinerComment: Melting and boiling points increase down Group VII, so astatine is a solid.

parts.prompt: State the two substances needed for iron to rust and explain how painting prevents rusting.

markingPoints.text: paint is a barrier that stops water and oxygen reaching the iron

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates knew the conditions for rusting.

parts.prompt: Name the main ore of iron.
parts.examinerComment: Bauxite, the ore of aluminium, was a common wrong answer.

questions.stem: A piece of metal X is placed in aqueous copper(II) sulfate. A brown solid forms on the metal and the blue colour of the solution fades.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain these observations.

markingPoints.text: X is more reactive than copper
X displaces copper / brown solid is copper
copper(II) ions are removed from solution so the blue colour fades

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers identified the brown solid as copper.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suggest a metal that could be X.
parts.examinerComment: Any metal above copper in the reactivity series, other than one that reacts with water, was accepted.

parts.prompt: Describe two stages in the treatment of the domestic water supply and state the purpose of each.

markingPoints.text: carbon to remove tastes and odours

parts.examinerComment: Each stage needed a correct purpose.

parts.prompt: Explain how carbon monoxide is formed in car engines and why it is harmful.

markingPoints.text: of carbon-containing fuels / petrol when there is not enough oxygen
it is toxic / reduces the ability of blood to carry oxygen

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates confused carbon monoxide with carbon dioxide.

parts.prompt: Explain how increasing amounts of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere lead to climate change.

markingPoints.text: carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas
absorbs thermal energy radiated from the Earth's surface
less energy escapes into space / energy is re-emitted back to Earth

parts.examinerComment: Answers that referred to holes in the ozone layer were not credited.

questions.stem: Ethene, C₂H₄, is made by cracking larger alkane molecules.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State two conditions used for cracking.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates knew that a high temperature is needed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Ethene is used to make poly(ethene). State the type of polymerisation and one problem caused by the disposal of plastics.

markingPoints.text: non-biodegradable / fills landfill sites / harms marine life / toxic gases when burned

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Name the two products of the complete combustion of methane.
parts.examinerComment: Carbon monoxide is formed only in incomplete combustion.

parts.prompt: Name the alkane with the molecular formula C₃H₈.
parts.examinerComment: Propene, C₃H₆, was a common error.

parts.prompt: A student does a titration. Two concordant titres are {a} cm³ and {=a+0.1} cm³. Calculate the mean titre, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates calculated the mean correctly. Titres should be given to 2 decimal places.

parts.prompt: Describe how pure water can be obtained from salt solution by simple distillation.

markingPoints.text: heat the solution so the water boils / evaporates
the steam is cooled in a condenser
water (distillate) is collected in a separate container
salt is left in the flask

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates described evaporation or filtration, which do not collect the water.

parts.prompt: Describe the test for oxygen gas, giving the result.
parts.examinerComment: A lighted splint 'popping' is the test for hydrogen.

parts.prompt: A gas syringe is sealed and the plunger is pushed in slowly at constant temperature. Explain, in terms of particles, what happens to the pressure of the gas.

markingPoints.text: particles are closer together / more particles per unit volume
particles collide with the walls more frequently

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers referred to the frequency of collisions with the container walls.

parts.prompt: Describe the changes in the arrangement, motion and energy of the particles when steam condenses to form liquid water.

markingPoints.text: particles move closer together / from far apart to touching
particles move more slowly / from fast random movement to sliding past each other
particles lose (kinetic) energy / energy is released

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates described the arrangement well but did not refer to energy.

parts.prompt: Explain why gases can be compressed easily but liquids cannot.

markingPoints.text: gas particles are far apart / large spaces between them
liquid particles are touching / close together

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Element Q has two isotopes, ⁶⁹Q and ⁷¹Q. In a sample of Q, {p}% of the atoms are ⁶⁹Q and the rest are ⁷¹Q. Calculate the relative atomic mass of Q in this sample. Give your answer to one decimal place.
parts.examinerComment: A common error was to average the two mass numbers without using the abundances.

parts.prompt: Describe the bonding in a molecule of nitrogen, N₂, and explain why nitrogen has a low boiling point.

markingPoints.text: triple covalent bond / three shared pairs of electrons
weak intermolecular forces / little energy needed to separate the molecules

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who wrote that covalent bonds are broken on boiling did not score the last mark.

parts.prompt: Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why copper is malleable and conducts electricity.

markingPoints.text: lattice of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons
layers of ions can slide over each other
delocalised electrons can move through the structure

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers referred to layers of positive ions rather than atoms or molecules.

parts.prompt: Iron is made by reducing iron(III) oxide: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. In a laboratory model, {=40*k} g of iron(III) oxide produces {=0.28*k*p} g of iron. Calculate the percentage yield of iron.
parts.examinerComment: The mole ratio of 1 : 2 was often missed, giving a yield above 100%, which should have alerted candidates to an error.

parts.prompt: A {m} g sample of impure limestone reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. The calcium carbonate in the sample produces {=2.4*m*p} cm³ of carbon dioxide, measured at r.t.p. The impurities do not react. Calculate the percentage purity of the calcium carbonate in the sample.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates forgot to convert cm³ to dm³ or did not divide by 24 000.

parts.prompt: {m} g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH, is dissolved in water and made up to {v} cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration of the solution, in mol/dm³.
parts.examinerComment: The volume must be in dm³.

parts.prompt: Magnesium reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Calculate the volume of hydrogen, measured at r.t.p., produced from {m} g of magnesium, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used the 1 : 2 ratio of Mg to HCl instead of the 1 : 1 ratio of Mg to H₂.

parts.prompt: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its relative molecular mass is 60. Deduce its empirical formula and molecular formula.

markingPoints.text: Mr of CH₂O = 30, so molecular formula C₂H₄O₂

parts.examinerComment: Well answered by candidates who showed each step of the working.

questions.stem: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed using inert electrodes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write the ionic half-equation for the reaction at the anode.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates wrote the electrons on the wrong side of the equation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why hydrogen, not sodium, is produced at the cathode.

markingPoints.text: sodium is more reactive than hydrogen
so hydrogen ions gain electrons / are reduced more readily than sodium ions

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers referred to the reactivity series.

parts.prompt: Write the overall equation for the reaction in a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell. Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using fuel cells instead of petrol engines in cars.

markingPoints.text: advantage: only product is water / no CO₂ or pollutants emitted
disadvantage: hydrogen is difficult to store or transport / hydrogen is often made using fossil fuels / few refuelling stations

parts.examinerComment: Vague answers such as 'better for the environment' did not score.

parts.prompt: Methane burns: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Use the bond energies to calculate the energy change for this reaction, in kJ/mol. Bond energies, in kJ/mol: C–H 435, O=O 498, C=O 805, O–H 464.
parts.examinerComment: The sign was often omitted. The value differs from the measured value because bond energies are average values.

parts.prompt: Ethanol burns: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O; ΔH = −1370 kJ/mol. Calculate the energy released when {m} g of ethanol burns completely, in kJ.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should give the energy released as a positive quantity, as the question asks for energy released.

parts.prompt: Explain, in terms of bond breaking and bond making, why the combustion of fuels is exothermic.

markingPoints.text: bond breaking is endothermic / takes in energy
bond making is exothermic / releases energy
more energy is released making bonds than is taken in breaking bonds

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates stated incorrectly that breaking bonds releases energy.

parts.prompt: Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid in a flask on a balance. The mass decreases by {d} g in the first {t} s. Calculate the average rate of reaction over this time, in g/s.
parts.examinerComment: The mass decreases because carbon dioxide escapes from the flask.

parts.prompt: Explain, in terms of activation energy and collisions, how a catalyst increases the rate of a reaction.

markingPoints.text: a greater proportion of particles have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
more successful collisions per unit time

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers referred to the frequency of successful collisions, not just 'more collisions'.

parts.prompt: Zinc reacts with aqueous copper(II) ions: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu. Explain, in terms of electrons and oxidation numbers, which species is oxidised, and identify the reducing agent.

markingPoints.text: oxidation number of zinc increases from 0 to +2, so zinc is oxidised

parts.examinerComment: The reducing agent is the species that is itself oxidised; many candidates named Cu²⁺.

parts.prompt: {v} cm³ of dilute sulfuric acid exactly neutralises 25.0 cm³ of {c} mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid, in mol/dm³.
parts.examinerComment: The 1 : 2 ratio was the main discriminator.

parts.prompt: Describe how to prepare a pure, dry sample of the insoluble salt barium sulfate by precipitation.

markingPoints.text: mix aqueous barium chloride / barium nitrate
with aqueous sodium sulfate / dilute sulfuric acid
dry in a warm oven / between filter papers

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates evaporated the filtrate, which is the method for soluble salts.

parts.prompt: Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid and ethanoic acid is a weak acid. Explain the difference, and compare the pH values of solutions of the two acids with the same concentration.

markingPoints.text: strong acid fully dissociates / ionises in water
hydrochloric acid has the lower pH / higher concentration of H⁺ ions

parts.examinerComment: Candidates often confused 'strong' with 'concentrated'.

parts.prompt: State three properties of transition elements that are not typical of Group I metals.
parts.examinerComment: Properties shared by all metals, such as conducting electricity, were not credited.

parts.prompt: Predict the formula of the compound formed when rubidium reacts with bromine.
parts.examinerComment: Group I forms 1+ ions and Group VII forms 1− ions.

parts.prompt: Helium is used to fill weather balloons. Give two reasons why helium is suitable.

markingPoints.text: low density / less dense than air

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Explain, using electronic configurations, why fluorine and chlorine have similar chemical properties.

markingPoints.text: both have seven electrons in their outer shell
both gain one electron when they react / they are in the same group

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates stated only that they are in the same group without referring to electrons.

parts.prompt: Zinc is extracted by heating zinc oxide with carbon: ZnO + C → Zn + CO. Calculate the maximum mass of zinc that can be produced from {m} kg of zinc oxide, in kg.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates can work in kg throughout because the units cancel.

parts.prompt: Describe how aluminium is extracted from purified aluminium oxide. Include the role of cryolite and explain why the anodes must be replaced regularly.

markingPoints.text: aluminium oxide dissolved in molten cryolite
cryolite lowers the operating temperature / reduces energy costs
oxygen forms at the (carbon) anode and reacts with it to form carbon dioxide

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers explained that the anodes are carbon and burn away.

parts.prompt: A galvanised steel bucket is scratched so that the steel is exposed. Explain why the steel still does not rust.

markingPoints.text: zinc is more reactive than iron
zinc loses electrons / is oxidised in preference to iron

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who described the zinc only as a barrier did not explain why scratched steel is protected.

parts.prompt: Describe three strategies that can reduce the effects of climate change.

markingPoints.text: use renewable energy / less fossil fuel combustion
reduce livestock farming / reduce methane emissions

parts.examinerComment: Strategies linked to acid rain or ozone were not credited.

parts.prompt: Explain how oxides of nitrogen are formed in car engines and how they lead to acid rain.

markingPoints.text: nitrogen and oxygen from the air react
at the high temperature in the engine
nitrogen dioxide dissolves in rain water / reacts with water and oxygen to form nitric acid

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Urea, CO(NH₂)₂, is used as a nitrogen fertiliser. Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in urea.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates counted only one nitrogen atom.

parts.prompt: Ethanol can be made by fermentation or by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene. Give the conditions for each method and one advantage of each.

markingPoints.text: addition of steam: about 300 °C, about 6000 kPa, acid catalyst
fermentation: uses renewable raw materials / low temperature
addition of steam: fast / continuous / pure product

parts.examinerComment: Candidates often gave conditions for only one method.

parts.prompt: Name the two structural isomers with the molecular formula C₄H₁₀ and state what is meant by structural isomers.

markingPoints.text: same molecular formula but different structural formulae

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates named butene, which has the formula C₄H₈.

parts.prompt: State two differences between addition polymerisation and condensation polymerisation.

markingPoints.text: addition: one product only / condensation: a small molecule such as water is also formed
addition monomers contain C=C / condensation monomers have two functional groups

parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers named the small molecule eliminated.

parts.prompt: Propane burns completely: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide, measured at r.t.p., produced when {m} g of propane burns, in dm³.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who omitted the 1 : 3 ratio lost the final two marks.

parts.prompt: Describe how aqueous ammonia can be used to distinguish between aqueous zinc sulfate and aqueous aluminium sulfate.

markingPoints.text: zinc hydroxide precipitate dissolves in excess aqueous ammonia (colourless solution)
aluminium hydroxide precipitate does not dissolve in excess

parts.examinerComment: Aqueous sodium hydroxide cannot distinguish them because both precipitates dissolve in excess.

parts.prompt: A student records three titres: 24.60 cm³, 23.85 cm³ and 23.95 cm³. Calculate the mean titre using only concordant results, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: The rough titre of 24.60 cm³ should be ignored.

parts.prompt: Amino acids are colourless. Explain how the spots are made visible on a chromatogram, and how the amino acids can be identified.

markingPoints.text: dry / heat so coloured spots appear
measure Rf values and compare with known values

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates suggested using ultraviolet light without naming a locating agent.
